title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-25
body:
Context:
- Intermittent throughput regression observed on prod-hosted cluster (eu-west-1) starting ~2026-02-18 03:00 UTC. Client-facing p95 latency spiked from 120ms -> 260ms and sustained token/sec dropped ~30% for 2 hours. No model change or config rollouts at that time according to rollout logs.

Hypothesis (working):
- Continuous batching misconfiguration interacting with KV-cache/sequence-length distribution creating smaller batches and more context loads per request.
- Autoscaler or packing policy regressed (lower batch window) -> lower GPU utilization.
- Recent kernel selection change (PR #1348) introduced a path that disables some batching coalescing for certain model sizes.

What I see in metrics: (short)
- avg batch size (tokens) dropped from 18 -> 11 during incident window (per-inference-metrics: batch_size_by_minute).
- avg GPU mem copy time + queue wait increased by ~22ms.
- KV cache hit ratio unchanged (~0.87) but effective reuse decreased for long-session traffic.

Commands I ran (local + prod shell snippets):
- Capture recent rollout history + env at time of incident:
  gcloud compute ssh infra-admin@orchestrator --command "kubectl get rollouts --namespace=redwood -o wide --sort-by=.status.startTime | tail -n 30"
  -> no rollouts in window except a small canary for observability agent.

- Query batch size timeseries (bigquery):
  bq query --nouse_legacy_sql '
    SELECT minute, AVG(batch_size) as avg_batch_size
    FROM `redwood-prod.metrics.batch`
    WHERE cluster="eu-west-1" AND minute BETWEEN TIMESTAMP("2026-02-18 02:00:00") AND TIMESTAMP("2026-02-18 06:00:00")
    GROUP BY minute ORDER BY minute
  '
  -> confirmed drop starting 03:00 UTC.

- Validate runtime config on nodes deployed 2026-02-18:
  kubectl -n redwood get pod -l app=runtime -o jsonpath='{"range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{.spec.containers[0].env}{"\n---\n"}{end}' | sed -n '1,120p'
  -> spotted env BATCHING_WINDOW_MS=5 on several nodes (expected 25).

Immediate observation: BATCHING_WINDOW_MS=5 is likely culprit (too aggressive). Need to confirm source of override.

Commands to find config source (done):
- Check configmap iteration history:
  kubectl -n redwood get configmap runtime-config -o yaml --export | sed -n '1,200p'
  git log --pretty=oneline -- config/runtime-config.yaml | head -n 20
  -> configmap was updated by infra/helm pipeline at 2026-02-17 23:59 UTC; change included packer defaults.

- Inspect helm values for recent chart versions:
  helm get values runtime-chart --namespace redwood --revision 45 > /tmp/values-r45.yaml
  grep -n "batchingWindow" /tmp/values-r45.yaml || true
  -> values-r45 has batching.windowMs: 5 in "packerMode: aggressive" block.

- Cross-check PRs: PR #1348 touched kernel selection; PR #1339 touched helm values for test env but accidentally merged packerMode: aggressive into prod values. See linked PR.

Error snippets / logs (excerpts):
- runtime pod stderr around incident:
  2026-02-18T03:02:35Z runtime[pid=1234] WARN batching: batch window expired size=7 wait_ms=5
  2026-02-18T03:02:35Z runtime[pid=1234] INFO batch_dispatch: dispatched 7 requests, expected_optimal=18, gpu_util=34%
  2026-02-18T03:02:35Z runtime[pid=1234] DEBUG kvcache: session_loads=482 queued=3 copy_us=2100

- Observability trace for a slow request:
  - trace_id: trace-0a1b
  - timeline: incoming->queue_wait(40ms)->batch_wait(5ms)->kernel_exec(190ms)->copy(8ms)
  kernel_exec was higher than typical 160ms. Possibly smaller batches -> worse per-token overhead.

Repro steps (dev env):
- Locally simulate stream with different BATCHING_WINDOW_MS:
  export BATCHING_WINDOW_MS=5; ./dev-server --mode=local --load-profile=prod-peak
  -> observed avg batch size 9, throughput down ~28% vs BATCHING_WINDOW_MS=25

- Try toggling packerMode in helm to "default":
  helm upgrade runtime-chart ./charts/runtime --set packerMode=default --namespace redwood --reuse-values --dry-run
  -> dry-run shows batching.windowMs=25 in rendered manifest. Plan: apply to a canary node pool.

Short-term mitigation applied (2026-02-19 09:20 UTC):
- Rolled packerMode back on 2 canary nodes: helm upgrade --set packerMode=default --namespace redwood --reuse-values runtime-chart
- Observed batch_size climb from 11 -> 17 on canary within 10 minutes; p95 latency decreased ~40ms.

Root cause (current best):
- Human error: packerMode=aggressive value (batches window reduced) was merged into prod helm values by PR #1339; combined with a recent kernel change this amplified the throughput impact. Not a single-code bug but config + new kernel tradeoff.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Why did config review not catch packerMode change? Add CI check to flag packerMode=aggressive for prod values.
- Does kernel PR #1348 need a mitigation for small-batch cases (e.g., fallback path to older kernel or adaptive packing)?
- Verify rollout protections so that helm pipeline cannot change packerMode in prod without manual approval.

Next steps (TODO):
- [ ] Create postmortem draft (link to incident JIRA INFRA-5421) and include timeline + mitigation.
- [ ] Add unit/integration test that simulates BATCHING_WINDOW_MS values and measures avg batch size delta to prevent accidental low-window merges.
- [ ] Add helm lint/gate to CI to block packerMode=aggressive in prod values.yml. (owner: Jordan)
- [ ] Revert kernel selection change or add small-batch tuning (owner: Samira)
- [ ] Run 48-hour watch on eu-west-1 after full rollout of default packerMode.

Notes to self:
- If regression recurs but config looks correct, instrument per-request "packing_reason" tag to see why requests are released early.
- Consider adding a periodic probe that sends long-session traffic to validate KV cache reuse rates.

Scratch timeline log (personal):
- 2026-02-18 03:10 UTC: first pager, paged oncall, started digging.
- 2026-02-18 04:00 UTC: identified batch size drop -> suspected packer changes.
- 2026-02-18 06:30 UTC: found BATCHING_WINDOW_MS env=5 on multiple pods.
- 2026-02-18 12:40 UTC: traced to helm values commit/PR #1339.
- 2026-02-19 09:20 UTC: applied canary rollback.
- 2026-02-20 11:00 UTC: canary stable, planning full rollout.

Appendix (useful snippets):
- Command to query batch size per-pod:
  kubectl -n redwood exec -it runtime-pod-abcdef -- /bin/sh -c '
    curl -s http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep batch_size_mean
  '
- Quick BQ query to correlate batch size -> p95 latency:
  SELECT minute, AVG(batch_size) AS avg_batch, PERCENTILE(latency_ms, 95) as p95
  FROM `redwood-prod.metrics.inference`
  WHERE cluster='eu-west-1' AND minute BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
  GROUP BY minute ORDER BY minute DESC LIMIT 100

Longer-term notes:
- Investigate adaptive batching: window can expand/contract based on recent queue backlog and GPU util. Might reduce sensitivity to manual config.
- Add a "safe-mode" that caps minimum batching window to 10ms for prod clusters.

End of scratchpad.

(Will convert into a cleaned-up incident postmortem once full timeline and artifacts collected.)
